clue.text: Crew observed in cutter

parts.note: a crew or gang of people can be called a band
observed means saw, past tense of see

explanation.surface: A ship's crew has been spotted aboard a small sailing cutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutter' looks like a boat to go with 'Crew', but it is a cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A power saw with a continuous toothed loop of steel is a tool for cutting wood or metal.

clue.text: Odds and ends I put in two forms of transport — another turns up

indicators.note: put in means the letter I is placed inside the transport words

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the old national railway
a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: another form of transport, here a car

explanation.surface: Miscellaneous items loaded into two vehicles, then a third appears.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, Britain's former state railway. 'Turns up' suits a down clue, where the reversed word reads upward; 'another' means another vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Small ornaments and trinkets of little value are miscellaneous oddments.

clue.text: Among finest ingredients, taking lots of eggs

indicators.note: among signals the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Among the finest cooking ingredients, a recipe using plenty of eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'fiNEST INGredients'; the eggs belong to a bird sitting on a clutch, not to a recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird sitting on its clutch in the nest is brooding a number of eggs.

clue.text: Conscious about maiden's romanticism

indicators.note: about means the word for conscious goes around the letter

parts.note: sentient means conscious, able to feel
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A girl fully aware of her own romantic leanings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts M (a maiden over in cricket) inside SENTIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentimentality and tender feeling are what romanticism in its soft sense amounts to.

clue.text: It sounds like what this engineer invented

indicators.note: the clue says the word that follows is matched by its pronunciation

parts.note: the word what is taken as written

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a famous engineer came up with.
explanation.walkthrough: James Watt, the Scottish engineer, improved the steam engine; his name is said like 'what'. 'This' and 'invented' are surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: James Watt was the Scottish inventor whose improved steam engine powered the Industrial Revolution.

clue.text: River crossed by burning bridges

parts.note: the stream Caesar crossed in 49 BC, a step that committed him irrevocably, just as burning your bridges leaves no way back

explanation.surface: A river spanned by bridges that are on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The crossing is a figure of speech: to 'cross' this Italian river means to take a step there is no going back from, the same idea as burning one's bridges.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar's crossing of this Italian stream started a civil war, so the name stands for any point of no return.

clue.text: Strand theatre's success has a reason

parts.note: a successful show has a long run
grounds are reasons, as in grounds for complaint

explanation.surface: A hit show in London's Strand theatre has its own explanation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strand' looks like the London street of theatres, but it is the verb, to beach a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To strand a ship is to beach it, leaving it stuck on the shore or a sandbank.

clue.text: Hardly the right audience response for villain

definitions.meaning: a cheer of well done, the opposite of the boos a stage villain should get
a hired thug or assassin, especially in old Italian usage

explanation.surface: Applauding the villain is hardly how a theatre audience should react.
explanation.definitionFit: A shout of approval is wrong for a stage baddie, and the same word names a hired cut-throat.

clue.text: Author mixed drink with ice

definitions.meaning: Wilkie ... wrote The Woman in White
the Tom version is gin, lemon juice, sugar and soda over ice

explanation.surface: A writer who mixes himself an iced drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilkie of that surname was a Victorian novelist, and the Tom cocktail of gin, lemon and soda bears the same name.

clue.text: Curious how the old boy's shown up

indicators.note: in a down clue shown up means read upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ye is an old form of the
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: How curious, the way the old boy has been exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shown up' reverses YESON. 'Old boy' looks like a former pupil, but 'the old' gives YE and 'boy' SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inquisitive about others' business is prying curiosity.

clue.text: Brand he created was a tragic failure

definitions.text: Brand he created was a tragic failure

parts.words: Brand he created was a tragic failure
parts.note: Brand is an 1865 verse play by a Norwegian dramatist, its hero a priest whose uncompromising faith ends in tragedy

explanation.surface: A marketer whose new brand flopped badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brand' reads like a commercial product, but it is the title of a play whose hero comes to a tragic end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian playwright wrote the drama Brand, about a priest destroyed by his own rigid ideals.

clue.text: Can settle? Put out feelers

indicators.note: letters put out are knocked out of place, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone told to settle a question sends out feelers to test opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' rearranges the letters of CAN SETTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus or snail feels its way with these long flexible organs, which are literally feelers.

clue.text: Defences produced by little boy getting the bird

parts.note: Al is a short form of the boy's name Albert or Alan
the ibis is a long-billed wading bird

explanation.surface: A little boy who was given the bird makes excuses for himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting the bird' suggests being booed; here it simply adds a bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An accused person's claims to have been elsewhere at the time are pleas offered in their defence.

clue.text: Move West from Wyoming in terrible disgrace

indicators.note: terrible signals that the letters are in a bad state and must be rearranged
from signals that something is taken out of the state's name that follows

parts.note: to move the West out is to take away W, the abbreviation for West

explanation.surface: Heading west out of Wyoming ends in a dreadful humiliation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move West from' takes W out of WYOMING to leave YOMING; with IN that makes YOMINGIN, which 'terrible' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignominy is public shame or dishonour, a synonym of disgrace.

clue.text: Stopped betting? It's beyond our ken

parts.note: closed means stopped or shut down
a bookmaker's book is the record of bets taken

explanation.surface: A bookmaker has stopped taking bets, for reasons nobody understands.
explanation.walkthrough: To make a book is to take bets on a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Something completely unknowable or mysterious to us is a subject we cannot open or read.

clue.text: Knave not found in pack

definitions.meaning: a knave is a scoundrel or rascal
a lone elephant or other animal that lives apart from the herd is called this

explanation.surface: A jack that is missing from the deck of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knave' and 'pack' suggest playing cards, but the second sense is an animal driven out of its herd.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is a rascal, and a solitary savage elephant living apart from its herd is described by the same word.

clue.text: Fierce females left one with zero points

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
O looks like the figure zero
a ness is a headland or promontory, a point of land

explanation.surface: A scoreboard shows one team left with no points at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' sounds like scoring but means headlands: a NESS is a promontory, as in Loch Ness's neighbour names around Britain's coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Female big cats that hunt for the pride are notoriously ferocious.

clue.text: Rugby chap comes to conclusion, as seen in 17

parts.note: Harry East is Tom's friend at Rugby School in Tom Brown's Schooldays
one who comes to a conclusion, finishing something, is an ender

explanation.surface: A rugby player reaches a conclusion, as shown in another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rugby' looks like the sport but is the English public school in Tom Brown's Schooldays. The definition points to 17: a resident of London's East End, as in the BBC TV serial named after them.
explanation.definitionFit: A Londoner from the East End is a character in the long-running BBC serial set in that area.

clue.text: Hence a popular time for programme

parts.note: hence means so, therefore
pop is short for popular
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Therefore a peak slot for a TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running domestic drama serial on television or radio is a kind of broadcast show.

clue.text: Woman who's kept score aunt, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that these letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A woman noting down a score for her aunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges SCORE AUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistress supported by a wealthy lover, historically at court, is a kept woman.

clue.text: Honourable, but not grand?

definitions.meaning: a piano with vertical strings, the other main type from a grand

explanation.surface: Someone decent but not especially grand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' looks like a social rank, but it is a grand piano; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: An honest person is morally straight, and a piano with vertical strings is the alternative to a grand.

clue.text: A bird once found in New Zealand, on South Island

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so the bird phrase follows the compass letter

parts.words: bird once found in New Zealand
parts.note: the moa was a huge flightless New Zealand bird, now extinct

explanation.surface: An extinct bird of New Zealand, located on the South Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South Island' looks like New Zealand's South Island, but 'South' gives S and 'Island' is the definition; 'on' places A MOA after S.
explanation.definitionFit: This Pacific nation is a group of islands, with Upolu and Savai'i the largest.

clue.text: Provide reference for one in French resort

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the resort name

parts.note: Menton is a resort on the French Riviera near Monaco
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Writing a job reference for someone staying at a French resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts I inside MENTON.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer to something in passing is to cite it, giving it a reference.

clue.text: If rebuffed, stay home

indicators.note: rebuffed means pushed back, so the word If is turned round

parts.note: to stay somewhere is to reside there

explanation.surface: If turned away, stay at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebuffed' turns IF into FI.
explanation.definitionFit: The hearth area of a house stands for home and domestic life, as in fireside comforts.

clue.text: Money not quite enough for author, composer or dictator

indicators.note: not quite means the name is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Anatole France the author, Franck the composer and General Franco the dictator all work

explanation.surface: Not quite enough cash to pay a writer, composer or tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: Each name shortened by its last letter gives the same result: FRANC(E), FRANC(K), FRANC(O).
explanation.definitionFit: The former currency of France, Belgium and still Switzerland is a unit of money.

clue.text: Book scholar found in ancient kingdom

parts.note: She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate or scholar

explanation.surface: A scholar's book discovered in an ancient kingdom's ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: SHE is H. Rider Haggard's adventure novel; BA is a Bachelor of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen of this realm visited Solomon in the Bible; it was an old Arabian state.

clue.text: Slow movement round ashed

annotationWithheld.why: Printed and held as 'Slow movement round ashed (4-2)': the scan also reads 'ashed', a slip for 'a shed' (LENTO round A, def shed); as held, 'ashed' would have to give A and be the definition at once

clue.text: Prophet's body turning up

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means read upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: soma is the body as opposed to the mind

explanation.surface: A prophet's corpse being found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' reverses SOMA; 'body turning up' suggests a corpse being discovered.
explanation.definitionFit: He was an Old Testament minor seer from Tekoa with a book of the Bible in his name.

clue.text: Variety of Low German used by fisherman

indicators.note: a variety of something is a different form of it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dialect of Low German spoken by a fisherman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety of' rearranges LOW GERMAN; 'Low German' looks like the dialect it really is.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers use earthworms as bait, and this is the old name for such a worm.

clue.text: Concerted effort to make ball go with a swing

definitions.meaning: an organised campaign, as in a fund-raising push

definitions.text: to make ball go with a swing
definitions.meaning: in golf or cricket, to hit the ball hard with a full swing of club or bat

explanation.surface: A team push to swing a ball hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign is an organised push, and a long hard shot off the tee in golf goes by the same word.

clue.text: Divide second prune

parts.note: to divide something is to cut it
to second a person is to support or back them

explanation.surface: A gardener's instruction: divide, then cut a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' is a verb here, to support, giving BACK.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim a plant hard is to reduce its growth, the same idea as a reduction in spending.

clue.text: Bloomer made by new government leader in republic

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round

parts.note: Syria is a Middle Eastern republic

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so government gives its opening letter

explanation.surface: A blunder by a newly elected head of government in some republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering shrub. 'In' puts N and G inside SYRIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac and mock orange go by this botanical name, both flowering shrubs.
